ANES Time Series Cumulative Data FileAbout · Using this site

About this site

This site describes the ANES Time Series Cumulative Data File, published by American National Election Studies. It is generated from the repository pdt-anes-cdf, which holds metadata built from the publisher's documentation: each variable's label, question text, codes and missing codes, and availability, with corrections and links between releases. Each fact says where it came from.

What it isn't

  • It isn't the publisher's site, and the publisher hasn't reviewed it. The publisher's own page for the dataset is https://electionstudies.org/data-center/anes-time-series-cumulative-data-file/. Where this site and the publisher's documentation differ, the publisher's documentation is the source; the differences this repository knows of are listed as corrections.
  • It doesn't hold the data. The data come from the publisher, or from this repository's data release when the terms allow; see Getting the data.
  • It makes no analysis decisions: which answers count as agreement, which weights or cases to use, or how to recode. Those belong to the projects that use the data.

Terms of use

Publisher's terms
https://electionstudies.org/data-center/
What they say
ANES's terms of use (Data Center page) say to use the data only for research or statistical purposes, make no use of respondents' identities, and cite ANES data and documentation. The FAQ says ANES public release datasets are public goods and that datasets created from them may be disseminated, with a link back to the original ANES dataset; restricted-use data may not. No login is needed to download. The pages don't address mirroring the original files or codebook, or LLM processing; Allen Downey decided both may ship. Copies of the pages are source anes-terms-pages.

PublicDataToolkit

The library and the standard that build this site: https://github.com/AllenDowney/PublicDataToolkit. This site was generated by version 0.1.0.

Reporting an error

  • In the publisher's documentation (a wrong label, a missing code, question text that belongs to another item): open an issue at the issue tracker of the repository pdt-anes-cdf, with where you found it. This repository records such errors as corrections, with the evidence, and keeps the publisher's original; it also says whether the error was reported to the publisher.
  • In this repository's records (a wrong link, a code classified wrongly, a variable left out): open an issue at the issue tracker of the repository pdt-anes-cdf.
  • To the publisher: American National Election Studies.
